problem_statement: Applications need to be able to override and extend the __ASSERT() macro globally, at the macro level, rather than only through the assert post-action hook. A new mechanism, equivalent to the custom-header options already used for logging and shell, must let an application-supplied header replace the __ASSERT macro so that a failing assert (e.g. __ASSERT(false, ...)) does not abort the program and instead invokes the assert post-action callback, allowing the code to continue running. When this custom-header option is enabled, a failed __ASSERT() must not crash the application but must still call the registered post-action handler.

verification.reason: The statement describes the desired behavior but omits the exact Kconfig option, the exact custom header name, and the required include behavior of the assert header needed by the hidden test.

problems.detail: The hidden test enables CONFIG_ASSERT_CUSTOM_HEADER=y, but the problem statement does not give this Kconfig option name.
The hidden test provides a custom header named zephyr_custom_assert.h and relies on it being included when the option is enabled; the statement does not give the exact header name.

The hidden test relies on the option causing the assert header include/zephyr/sys/__assert.h to include the custom header after the default __ASSERT definition so it can replace __ASSERT; the statement does not specify this interface behavior.

leak_check.leak_detail: The phrase saying that code that includes zephyr/sys/__assert.h must also include zephyr_custom_assert.h as part of the assert subsystem's public header interface closely mirrors the fix's include in __assert.h, though it can be read as a public interface requirement rather than an internal implementation step.
leak_check.missing: It does not explicitly state that the custom header must be included after the existing __ASSERT definitions, i.e. at the end of __assert.h, so the application's redefinition takes effect.
leak_check.suggested_statement: Applications need to be able to override and extend the __ASSERT() macro globally, at the macro level, rather than only through the assert post-action hook. A new Kconfig option named CONFIG_ASSERT_CUSTOM_HEADER, equivalent to the custom-header options already used for logging and shell, must let an application-supplied header named zephyr_custom_assert.h replace the __ASSERT macro so that a failing assert such as __ASSERT(false, ...) does not abort the program and instead invokes the assert post-action callback, allowing the code to continue running. When CONFIG_ASSERT and CONFIG_ASSERT_CUSTOM_HEADER are enabled, the public assert header interface must make zephyr_custom_assert.h available to code that includes zephyr/sys/__assert.h, so the application header can redefine __ASSERT and use existing assert post-action macros such as __ASSERT_POST_ACTION. With this option enabled, a failed __ASSERT() must not crash the application but must still call the registered post-action handler, assert_post_action, through __ASSERT_POST_ACTION.
